canonical.title: Server-driven data: which React table actually does the work for you

parent.title: Which React table component to use in 2026

siblings.title: The 2026 React table landscape: headless vs batteries-included vs commercial grid
siblings.summary: Only four candidates are genuinely alive in 2026 — TanStack Table, AG Grid, MUI X Data Grid and react-data-grid — and the real axis is not features but how many weeks of table you agree to write yourself.

siblings.title: React tables at row scale: where the ceilings actually are
siblings.summary: Row count is almost never the constraint that breaks a React grid — update frequency, referential stability and the browser's 33.5M-pixel scroll cap are.

siblings.title: Enterprise React data-grid features and what they actually cost in 2026
siblings.summary: AG Grid Enterprise at $999/dev perpetual is the cheapest way to buy row grouping + pivot + Excel export; building the same on TanStack Table costs 25-50 dev-days, so buy wins below ~40 developers.

siblings.title: Styling and design-system fit: which React grid bends to your design system?
siblings.summary: If the design system is authoritative, go headless (TanStack Table, or shadcn's copy-paste wiring of it); grid-owned CSS is only worth it when you're buying AG Grid's feature set, and MUI X / Mantine grids are design-system adoptions, not component adoptions.

sources.title: TanStack Table — Pagination guide
sources.claim: manualPagination makes the table assume data is already paginated; you must supply rowCount or pageCount (-1 for unknown), and autoResetPageIndex is disabled automatically.

sources.title: TanStack Table — Column Filtering guide
sources.claim: manualFiltering disables built-in filtering logic; the table uses the data you pass as-is.

sources.title: TanStack Table v8 — Sorting guide
sources.claim: manualSorting tells the table the data is already sorted and to apply no sorting itself.

sources.title: TanStack Table — Grouping guide
sources.claim: manualGrouping exists but TanStack Table has no practical server-side grouping story.

sources.title: TanStack Table issue #4797 — manualPagination doesn't reset pageIndex
sources.claim: With manualPagination + manualFiltering, pageIndex is not reset to 0 when column filters change; the user stays on page 1000 and gets empty results. Open issue.

sources.title: TanStack Table V9 Taking Form
sources.claim: TanStack Table V9 entered beta on 7 June 2026 with TanStack Store state, plugin-registered features, and large memory/type wins; no change to the server-side manual model.

sources.title: TanStack Table — Virtualized Infinite Scrolling example
sources.claim: Official TanStack example combines react-table, react-query useInfiniteQuery and react-virtual for virtualized infinite scroll.

sources.title: TanStack Query — Paginated Queries guide
sources.claim: placeholderData: keepPreviousData keeps the last successful fetch visible across query-key changes and swaps seamlessly; isPlaceholderData gates the Next button.

sources.title: TanStack Query — Migrating to v5
sources.claim: TanStack Query v5 removed keepPreviousData and isPreviousData in favour of placeholderData and isPlaceholderData.

sources.title: TanStack Query — Infinite Queries guide
sources.claim: Cursor pagination uses useInfiniteQuery with getNextPageParam returning the server's next cursor; maxPages caps retained pages.

sources.title: SWR — Pagination
sources.claim: SWR 2.x keepPreviousData: true keeps prior data when the key changes, the SWR equivalent of Query's keepPreviousData for paginated tables.

sources.title: AG Grid — Server-Side Row Model
sources.claim: AG Grid SSRM lazy-loads rows and groups; getRows request carries startRow/endRow, sortModel, filterModel, rowGroupCols, groupKeys, valueCols, pivotCols; filtering, sorting, grouping, pivoting and aggregation execute on the server.

sources.title: AG Grid — Row Models
sources.claim: AG Grid has four row models; Client-Side and Infinite are Community, Server-Side and Viewport are Enterprise. SSRM is recommended over Infinite for Enterprise customers.

sources.title: AG Grid — Server-Side Datasource
sources.claim: IServerSideDatasource.getRows(params) responds via params.success({rowData, rowCount}) or params.fail().

sources.title: AG Grid — Infinite Row Model
sources.claim: Infinite Row Model cannot group or aggregate; cacheBlockSize defaults to 100, maxBlocksInCache evicts LRU, blockLoadDebounceMillis suppresses fetches while scrolling, and sort/filter changes purge the cache and refetch.

sources.title: AG Grid blog — Using AG Grid with Next.js
sources.claim: AG Grid React cannot be server-rendered; it needs 'use client' because it depends on browser APIs.

sources.title: How to integrate React Query with AG Grid
sources.claim: You cannot call useQuery inside AG Grid's getRows; use useQueryClient() and queryClient.fetchQuery inside the datasource, memoise it, and include all request params in the query key.

sources.title: MUI X — Server-side data (Data Source)
sources.claim: GridDataSource.getRows receives filterModel, sortModel, paginationModel, start/end, groupKeys, aggregationModel; the grid handles caching (GridDataSourceCacheDefault, 5-min TTL, swappable via dataSourceCache), errors via onDataSourceError, dataSourceKeepPreviousData and dataSourceRevalidateMs polling.

sources.title: MUI X — Server-side lazy loading
sources.claim: Server-side lazy loading requires Data Grid Pro; known rowCount gives viewport loading with skeleton rows and a 500ms request throttle, rowCount=-1/undefined gives infinite loading at scroll-end.

sources.title: MUI X — Server-side aggregation
sources.claim: Server-side aggregation is a Premium-plan feature using aggregationModel in getRows plus a getAggregatedValue() getter on GridDataSource.

sources.title: MUI X — Pagination
sources.claim: paginationMode="server" + rowCount + onPaginationModelChange is the manual path; rowCount going undefined during loading resets the page to zero; unknown counts use rowCount={-1} with paginationMeta.hasNextPage or estimatedRowCount.

sources.title: MUI X — DataGrid API
sources.claim: The MIT Community DataGrid exposes paginationMode, sortingMode and filterMode ('client' | 'server', default 'client') and a dataSource prop of type { getRows, updateRow? }.

sources.title: MUI X v8 release blog
sources.claim: MUI X v8 moved the Data Source into the Community (MIT) plan and added server-side aggregation, infinite scrolling and lazy loading on top of it.

sources.title: Mantine React Table — Pagination guide
sources.claim: Mantine React Table exposes manualPagination and requires you to override pageCount/rowCount and manage pagination state yourself, fetching in a useEffect.

sources.title: Mantine React Table — GitHub
sources.claim: Mantine React Table is a Mantine wrapper around TanStack Table V8; latest tagged release is v1.3.3 from October 2023.

sources.title: nuqs — Server-side usage
sources.claim: createSearchParamsCache parses searchParams in a Server Component and propagates typed values down the RSC tree without prop drilling; parsers are shared with client useQueryStates.

sources.title: nuqs — GitHub
sources.claim: nuqs useQueryState with shallow:false notifies the server to re-render Server Components; throttleMs rate-limits URL writes and server requests while hook state updates instantly (default 50ms, ~340ms on Safari).

sources.title: shadcn-table — GitHub
sources.claim: Reference implementation of TanStack Table + Next.js with server-side pagination, sorting and filtering, advanced filter menus and virtualized infinite scroll.

sources.title: Next.js — Server and Client Components
sources.claim: Marking a file 'use client' pulls it and everything it imports/renders into the client bundle; React context is unavailable in Server Components.

sources.title: React — useEffect reference
sources.claim: Network responses may arrive out of order; the ignore-flag cleanup guards against it, and React recommends a framework's data fetching or TanStack Query / SWR instead of hand-rolled effects.

sources.title: Robin Wieruch — React server-side table
sources.claim: Without debouncing a server-side table fires a request per keystroke; you must own and coordinate search, filter and pagination state yourself and merge them into every request.
